This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the 8th accused in Crime No.1042 of 2025 of Museum Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 23 and 5 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019.

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. According to the prosecution, the first accused M/s.FARMFED Southern Multi State Co-operative Society Ltd. had, along with other accused, induced the de facto complainant and her husband to make deposits in the company promising to provide 12.5% interest per month and though they deposited a total amount of Rs.16 Lakhs, the accused failed to pay the interest or return the principle amount and thereby committed the offences alleged.

entities.text: FARMFED Southern Multi State Co-operative Society Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Heard Sri.Sarin Panicker, the learned Counsel for the petitioner as well as Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner has been falsely arrayed as an accused and that she has no involvement in the alleged crime and, therefore, she may be granted anticipatory bail.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.
7. Petitioner is the Manager of the first accused company.
Petitioner's role to disburse the interest or return the amount is limited.
As a Manager, prima facie she has no authority to disburse any amount due to any person from the aforesaid company.
In such circumstances, I am of the view that petitioner could be protected with an order of pre-arrest bail.

8. In Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another, 2020 (5) SCC 1, it was held that while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant,
and the 2025:KER:59867 facts of the case.

and subject to the discretion of the court.

sentences.text: Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the view that petitioner is entitled to be released on pre-arrest bail.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 20.08.2025 and shall subject herself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner,
then, she shall be released on bail on her executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall she tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while she is on bail.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.

Sd/-
